_meta.name: views
_meta.what: How an element is shown, by its kind. Presentation data, not the standard. A kind with no row draws as its type draws today, in the standard's section order. Each tool keeps its own drawing and reads the row: a tool's own words for a heading or a fold are its drawing, and a fold's label is the word a tool uses where it has none of its own; which fields it draws, in what order, open or folded, are the row's. Nothing here says who may see or do what (that is the server's, by what it serves).
_meta.match: A row's kind is a type alone, a type with a supertype, or a profile's pair, which matches only with that profile's mark, by that profile's own reader (room: isRoomElement in npm, is_room_element in Python; charter: isCharterElement, is_charter_element). Types and supertypes are trimmed and folded as profiles/room.md defines once. The most specific row wins: a profile's pair, then a type with a supertype, then a type alone. No two rows hold the same kind: a file where two do is at fault, and is refused where it is built. A reader drawing a page never refuses over the table: where two rows match on one rung, the first in the file wins. An element no row matches has no row and draws as its type; the banners still show.
_meta.sentence: The card's, a list row's and a hover's one sentence: the first field named in the row's `sentence` whose value is a string that holds something after trimming; that value trimmed, cut at its first line break (U+000A or U+000D), and trimmed again, whitespace being the room profile's White_Space set. A field whose value is not a string holds nothing. No field holds anything: no sentence. This says what the sentence is where a tool shows one; a tool that shows names only need show none.
_meta.banners: Marks a served body carries, shown at the head of every kind's page in the order of the `banners` list, each read as the page or document named defines it: `known_of` and `hidden` only when true, the two review marks only when the value is an object with something in it (profiles/review.md: an empty mark is settled, rule 1; an object with at least one key is a mark whatever its keys, rule 5; a reader that shows a world to its people ignores a value that is not an object, rule 4), and `x_served_trimmed` only when it names a field (its list holds at least one string with something left after trimming: a list of blanks shows no banner). A row's own `banner` adds to them, after them, each read by presence as the room profile reads a mark: not null, a string only when something is left after trimming, any other value counts. Three of them are onlyworlds.com's own, not the standard's, and say so: a reader on another platform may never see them.

banners.defined_by: onlyworlds.com, not the standard: a known-of stub, known_of: true (the API document, https://www.onlyworlds.com/api/v2/openapi.json)
onlyworlds.com, not the standard: hidden: true, served only to readers who still see the element (the API document, https://www.onlyworlds.com/api/v2/openapi.json)
onlyworlds.com, not the standard: ids the server left out of a list, the field named (the API document, https://www.onlyworlds.com/api/v2/openapi.json; profiles/message.md reads it)

layouts.document: the fields in the row's order, each drawn once: lead open, then the rest, then fold; a field the row names in both lead and fold is drawn in the lead. The rest are the type's section fields in the schema's own order (schema/<type>.yaml: its sections as listed, and each section's fields as listed) that the row puts in neither lead nor fold. A generic link (a Pin's `element`) is one field of the order, under its schema name and at its place, never its two keys as two entries: it is read as the two keys schema.json gives it (`type_key`, `id_key`), and it holds something only when both are strings with something left after trimming; one alone, or both empty, holds nothing. A field that holds nothing (absent, null, a string with nothing left after trimming, a list with no items, an object with no keys; a list of blank strings holds something here, whatever a banner reads of one) is not drawn: an empty lead field is skipped, and a fold whose field holds nothing draws no fold. A tool that draws empty fields to be filled draws them at their own place in this order; it never moves a field. The base fields outside every section (name, description, supertype, subtype, image_url) are the page's head, unless the row names one in lead or fold, where it is drawn, and only there. A row names only the type's base and section fields, never an extension key, and extension keys and a world's own fields are not in the order. A kind with no row is a document.
layouts.conversation: the element within its chain by the named link, oldest first by created_at, read and ordered as profiles/message.md orders messages, stopping at an id already visited; each line's own fields drawn as a document draws them; a tool that shows one element and no thread draws that element as a document, and this layout asks nothing of it
